items.title: WIP: feat(pulls): add global pull request listing and review
items.body:
Add a global PR scope that searches pull requests across all readable
repositories on the selected Gitea instance without requiring local Git
discovery. Support repository owner/name fields, efficient
issue-search-backed rendering, optional detail loading, CI status
lookup, pagination, and graceful handling of inaccessible repositories.

Extend interactive review to select an open PR globally, including
pagination and selection of the target repository. Guard global-only
flags and invalid combinations, update CLI documentation and examples,
and add coverage for global listing, review selection, degraded results,
validation, and repository-aware CI output.

Fixes: https://gitea.com/gitea/tea/issues/1116

items.title: feat(login): support TLS client certificates for mutual TLS servers
items.body:
Gitea instances behind a reverse proxy that requires mutual TLS (nginx'
ssl_verify_client, or the equivalent in Traefik or HAProxy) reject every
tea request at the proxy, before it reaches Gitea. The user sees an opaque
403/400 from the proxy rather than an authentication error, and there was
no way to make tea present a certificate: only full verification and
--insecure were configurable.

Add an optional client certificate to a login, stored as client_cert and
client_key next to the existing insecure flag:

    tea login add --url https://git.example.com --token ... \
        --client-cert ~/.certs/client.crt \
        --client-key ~/.certs/client.key

The pair is loaded by Login.TLSConfig(), which now builds the TLS config
for every outgoing connection: SDK API calls, the OAuth authorization and
token refresh flows, and the raw 'tea api' client. Because the certificate
lives on the login, all commands using it present it automatically. Paths
support ~ expansion so they can be written into the config file by hand,
and clones pass the same material to git as http.sslCert/http.sslKey.

Both fields must be set together; setting only one, or pointing at a
certificate that cannot be loaded, is a hard error rather than a silent
fallback to a plain connection, which would fail at the proxy with the
same opaque error the certificate is meant to avoid.

Requests without either setting keep Go's default TLS behaviour: the
config is only overridden when the login asks for it.

Fixes #451

items.title: feat(pulls): offer to delete the source branch after merging
items.body:
Implements #1050.

After a successful `tea pr merge`, tea prompts whether to delete the pull request's source branch, naming it in the prompt. `--delete-branch` skips the prompt for scripts (#810).

## Changes

- Add `PullDeleteBranch` to delete the head branch via the API on the head repository, supporting unfetched forks (unlike `tea pr clean`, which requires a local checkout).
- Delete matching local branches best-effort by commit rather than name to preserve unpushed commits, matching `PullClean` behavior.
- Gate the prompt on stdin and stdout being terminals; `IsInteractiveMode` only checks `NumFlags() == 0`, which causes non-interactive `tea pr merge <idx>` invocations to hang.
- Explicitly handle already-deleted branches, open pull requests, and missing push permission.

## Tests

- Table-driven tests using `httptest` for API paths and a temporary git repository for local cleanup.
- `make vet`, `make lint`, `make fmt-check`, `make docs-check`, `make unit-test` pass.

The issue author offered to implement this but hasn't, and there is no open PR for it.
